claim: Sint-Martens-Bodegem has its own SNCB station on the Brussels regional rail network.
quote: Sint-Martens-Bodegem station : facilities and access

claim: The direct train from Sint-Martens-Bodegem to Brussels-Central runs hourly and takes about 28 minutes over a 9-mile distance.
quote: The distance between Sint-Martens-Bodegem Station and Brussels Central Station is 9 miles. There is a direct train departing from Sint-Martens-Bodegem and arriving at Bruxelles-Central, with services departing hourly every day, and the journey takes approximately 28 minutes.

claim: Sint-Martens-Bodegem is served by S-trains S4 and S10 of the Brussels regional express network (GEN/RER).
quote: Sint-Martens-Bodegem is a stop on lines S4 and S10 of the Regional Express Network (GEN) around Brussels.

claim: Brussels' Grand Place is a UNESCO-listed central square ringed by guildhalls, the Town Hall and the King's House, and is the natural starting point for a city visit.
quote: The Grand Place is a UNESCO World Heritage site and the vibrant heart of Brussels... captivating visitors with its opulent guildhalls, the stunning Town Hall, and the unique King's House.

claim: Visit Brussels lists the Grand Place, Manneken Pis, the Royal Galleries of Saint Hubert and the Atomium among the city's must-see attractions.
quote: Must-see attractions in Brussels | Visit Brussels

claim: The Atomium, built for the 1958 World Expo, is 102 metres tall and offers panoramic views of Brussels from its top sphere.
quote: The Atomium, with a maximum height of 102 metres, represents an iron crystal and was inaugurated in 1958. At the top sphere, visitors are rewarded with panoramic views stretching across Brussels.

claim: The Royal Palace of Brussels was closed in 2025 for renovation and is expected to reopen to visitors in summer 2026.
quote: The Royal Palace was closed to visitors in 2025 due to renovations, with visits expected to resume in summer 2026.

claim: Visit Flanders pitches Leuven as a 48-hour itinerary destination centred on its university, historic core and student-driven nightlife.
quote: 48 hours in Leuven: knowledge, culture and a vibrant student population

claim: Leuven sits roughly 25 minutes by direct train from Brussels' main stations, making it an easy day trip.
quote: Leuven is just 25 minutes by train from Brussels, making it an ideal day trip destination.

claim: Leuven's Grote Markt is dominated by the Brabantine Gothic Town Hall (foundation laid 1439) and the late-Gothic St Peter's Church, a UNESCO belfry site restored in 2020.
quote: the monumental Town Hall where the first stone was laid in 1439... Saint Peter's Church is a 15th-century late-Gothic monument with belfry that has been a UNESCO world heritage site since 1999 and was fully restored in 2020.

claim: The University Library tower offers a 360-degree viewing platform; the iLUVLeuven combination ticket (€17) bundles the library, a Town Hall guided tour and either M Museum or Park Abbey.
quote: the 360-degree viewing platform allows you to see Leuven and the surrounding countryside... For €17, you can pick up an iLUVLeuven Ticket, which includes entry to University Library, a Town Hall guided tour, and either M Museum or Park Abbey.

claim: St Rumbold's Cathedral in Mechelen is open Mon–Sat 08:30–17:30 and Sun 13:00–17:30 with free entry, and houses Van Dyck's 'Christ on the Cross' plus Lucas Faydherbe's 1665 high altar.
quote: Monday 08:30 - 17:30... Sunday 13:00 - 17:30... Anthony van Dyck's painting 'Christ on the Cross'... the high altar by Lucas Faydherbe which dates from 1665.

claim: The St Rumbold's Tower ascent involves over 500 steps to a 97-metre-high Skywalk with city panorama and carillon views, ticket around €8.
quote: the 97-meter-high Skywalk on top and the climb to reach it guarantee a unique experience. The climb involves over 500 steps for panoramic city views and a close-up look at the impressive carillon.

claim: Mechelen's compact historic centre with its UNESCO-listed Belfort on Grote Markt can be covered in one full day from Brussels.
quote: One full day is enough to see Mechelen's main attractions, including Grote Markt, St. Rumbold's Cathedral tower climb, and the key museums, with the compact historic centre making it perfect for a day trip from Antwerp or Brussels.

claim: Aalst sits on the Dender in East Flanders and is best known for its annual UNESCO-listed satirical carnival held in February or March.
quote: Aalst is a lively city in East Flanders, Belgium, known for its rich history, vibrant traditions, and warm, welcoming atmosphere, situated along the River Dender.

claim: The Carnival of Aalst was removed from the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2019 after the mayor asked for delisting amid antisemitic-imagery controversy; key traditions include the Voil Jeanetten cross-dress parade, the Ajuinworp onion throw and an effigy burning to close the three days before Ash Wednesday.
quote: Men walk around in women's clothes and props such as a bird cage, a herring, fake breasts, corsets, a fur coat, a worn out umbrella and a stroller.

claim: The 2026 Aalst Carnival runs from Sunday 15 February 2026, with the city otherwise reachable in about 30 minutes by direct train from Brussels.
quote: In 2026, the Aalst carnival starts on Sunday, February 15th.

claim: Year-round Aalst draws are the 15th-century Belfry attached to the old Town Hall, the Gothic Saint Martin's Church and the Stedelijk Museum focused on textiles, civic life and carnival history.
quote: The Belfry of Aalst is a striking symbol of the city's medieval heritage, a UNESCO-listed tower, part of the old Town Hall, dating back to the 15th century.

claim: Ninove is a small Dender-side town in East Flanders whose centrepiece is the Baroque Onze-Lieve-Vrouw Hemelvaartkerk (former Norbertine abbey church) consecrated in 1727 with a hexagonal-lantern tower added in 1825–1844.
quote: The Abbey Church (Onze-Lieve-Vrouw Hemelvaartkerk) was part of the Norbertine Abbey of Saint Cornelius and Saint Cyprianus, founded in 1137... This three-aisled baroque church was consecrated in 1727.

claim: Ninove's other listed sights cluster around the neoclassical Oud Stadhuis (1834) and the Dender riverfront, marketed as a low-key half-day stop rather than a full-day destination.
quote: THE 15 BEST Things to Do in Ninove (2026)

claim: Groot-Bijgaarden Castle in Dilbeek itself hosts the spring Floralia Brussels flower exhibition with millions of tulip, daffodil and hyacinth bulbs in its grounds.
quote: Groot-Bijgaarden Castle: Floralia Brussels Entry Ticket

claim: Dilbeek's other in-village attractions are the moated 12th-century Groot-Bijgaarden Castle, the De Viron Castle (now town hall) with its public park, and the green Pede Valley hiking area.
quote: De Viron Castle was originally built for the De Viron family and has been used as a family residence and town hall; today it houses the administrative offices of the municipality of Dilbeek.

claim: Gaasbeek Castle is open Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00 from 1 April to 15 November 2026 (closing 17:00 from October; museum garden 1 May–31 Oct), closed Mondays and 18–25 June for exhibition setup.
quote: Open from April 1 to November 15, 2026 ... exceptionally closed from 18 to 25 June ... 10 am to 6 pm (closing at 5 pm from October onward). Closed Mondays.

claim: Gaasbeek's 2026 programme features 'The Attic of Arnoldus the Mouse' for families in April–May and a Clara Spilliaert solo exhibition from 26 June to 15 November 2026.
quote: In April and May 2026, families with children can enjoy 'The Attic of Arnoldus the Mouse' ... From June 26 to November 15, 2026, artist Clara Spilliaert will have her first solo museum exhibition.

claim: Gaasbeek Castle sits between the hills of the Pajottenland, a short drive south-west of Brussels.
quote: Gaasbeek Castle lies between the hills of Pajottenland, not far from bustling Brussels.

claim: Cantillon in Anderlecht offers self-guided visits Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat 10:00–16:00 (shop 17:00), with Saturday 90-minute guided tours at €13 (online booking required); closed Wed, Sun and public holidays.
quote: M/Tu/Th/Fr/Sa: Visits and drinks from 10AM to 4PM (shop open till 5PM) ... Every Saturday guided tours ... Online booking is REQUIRED. Price: € 13.00 p.p.

claim: 3 Fonteinen's Lambik-O-Droom tasting room in Beersel opens Fri/Sat 14:00–20:30 and Sun 13:00–19:30, with free guided tours Fri/Sat at 15:00 and Sun at 14:00 (no reservation, max 20).
quote: Guided tours take place every Friday and Saturday at 3:00 PM, and every Sunday at 2:00 PM ... Participation is free of charge, with a maximum of 20 attendees.

claim: Brouwerij Boon in Lembeek runs 1-hour individual tours every Saturday at 14:00 with a 3-beer tasting for €13, plus the BOON Bar (13:00–19:00) and shop.
quote: Individual tours take place every Saturday at 2pm, last 1 hour, and include a tasting of 3 beers for €13 per person.

claim: Oud Beersel offers brewery visits with mandatory online reservation every Saturday at 11:00 (Dutch) and 12:00 (English).
quote: You can visit the brewery with mandatory online reservation every Saturday of the month at 11 am (Dutch) and at 12h (English).

claim: Mort Subite in Kobbegem (Asse), only ~10 km from Sint-Martens-Bodegem, hosts guided visits by appointment on weekdays except Friday (last tour 14:00); a tour is ≤1h brewery + ≤1h tasting.
quote: guided tours available on weekdays except Friday, and the last tour starting at 14:00. Reservations must be made via email. A tour consists of a brewery visit (max. 1 hour) followed by a tasting (max. 1 hour).

claim: Toer de Geuze 2026 — a free biennial open-doors weekend across 14 HORAL lambic producers including Boon, Lindemans, Mort Subite, Oud Beersel, Timmermans, Tilquin and De Cam — runs Sat 9 and Sun 10 May 2026 (Sat 11:00–19:00, Sun 10:00–17:00).
quote: next edition of the Toer de Geuze will take place on Saturday, May 9 and Sunday, May 10, 2026 ... opening hours are from 11 AM to 7 PM on Saturday and from 10 AM to 5 PM on Sunday.

claim: The Brussels Museum of the Gueuze is integrated into the working Cantillon brewery, doubling as a living archive of lambic history and production; €25 annual membership gives free tour access and shop discounts.
quote: the museum is fully integrated into the brewery and serves as a way to inform visitors of both the history of Cantillon as well as the production process ... membership for the fee of €25.

claim: The Bruegelwandeling is an 8 km signposted walk through Sint-Anna-Pede (Dilbeek) lasting roughly 3 hours, passing 11 weatherproof reproductions of Bruegel paintings including 'Parable of the Blind' and 'Peasant Wedding'.
quote: 8 km walking route in Sint-Anna-Pede (Dilbeek) featuring 11 large, weather-resistant color reproductions of Pieter Bruegel's paintings, taking approximately 3 hours to complete.

claim: Dilbeek presents the Pedevallei around Sint-Anna-Pede as an open-air 'Bruegel's Eye' landscape museum, conserving the rolling rural views that inspired the 16th-century painter.
quote: Bruegel's Eye: reconstructing the landscape

claim: The Bruegel walk starts at Sint-Anna church (the building immortalised in 'The Blind Leading the Blind') and crosses under 'The 17 Bridges' viaduct, a 520 m long, 28 m high 1932 concrete railway bridge over the Pedebeek valley.
quote: the 520 metre long viaduct known locally as 'The 17 bridges.' The viaduct was completed in 1932 as part of the work to build a new express railway line between Ghent ... and Brussels.

claim: Herisem Paper Mill in Alsemberg opens to individuals Sundays 14:00–17:00 (closed mid-July–early August and 1 Dec–29 Feb); weekday visits by reservation; the ~1h30 guided tour includes a handmade-paper demonstration, with steam-engine demos on the first Sunday of June and third Sunday of November.
quote: Sundays: 2:00 PM – 5:00 PM ... Steam engine demonstrations occur on the first Sunday of June and third Sunday of November (2:00 PM – 5:00 PM).

claim: Herisem in Alsemberg is described as an authentic 16th-century paper mill and 19th-century industrial complex, considered a national landmark of Belgian industrial archaeology.
quote: an authentic example of a 16th century paper mill and a 19th century industrial complex, serving as a national treasure of industrial archeology.

claim: Pajottenland is the rural belt south-west of Brussels in Flemish Brabant — covering Dilbeek, Gooik, Lennik, Galmaarden, Pepingen, Roosdaal, Bever and Halle — known for lambic beer, working watermills and the Bruegel landscape.
quote: Pajottenland

claim: The Regionaal Landschap Pajottenland & Zennevallei actively conserves the region's historic water- and windmills as part of its 'Water en Wind' heritage programme.
quote: Water en Wind | Regionaal landschap Pajottenland & Zennevallei

claim: Hallerbos hosts a 2026 Bluebell Festival with free shuttle from Halle station and free bicycle rental on weekends/holidays during the bloom period.
quote: On April 11, 12, 18, 19, 25, 26 and May 1, there is a free shuttle bus between Halle 'Stationsplein' and Parking 2 every half hour from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Saturdays and every 20 minutes on Sundays and May 1.

claim: Hallerbos bluebells bloom mid-April through early May 2026, with the forest floor turning into a blue carpet; by late May/June the bloom is finished but the forest remains beautiful year-round.
quote: The forest floor will be transformed into a colorful, blue-hued carpet until the start of May 2026.

claim: The Sonian Forest (Zoniënwoud) has a yellow-marked walking network with green-circle starting points at entrance gates and is accessible by train via Groenendaal, Hoeilaart or Lahulpe stations.
quote: You can map out your own walking trail in the Sonian Forest thanks to the route planner of RouteYou. The overview map shows the walking network with yellow lines marking hiking paths and green circles indicating starting points at entrance gates.

claim: A new United Nations Sonian Forest Trail opened on 20 October 2024, offering an additional themed walking option in the Zoniënwoud.
quote: A new UN trail in the Sonian Forest was opened on 20 October 2024.

claim: The Bruegelwandeling is a signposted 8 km loop (~3 hours) starting at Sint-Anna-Pede in Dilbeek with 11 weather-resistant Bruegel painting reproductions through the Pede valley.
quote: The well-signposted 8 km walking route takes approximately 3 hours and starts in Sint-Anna-Pede in Dilbeek... 11 large, weather-resistant colored reproductions of paintings by Pieter Bruegel the Elder.

claim: Provinciaal Domein Huizingen is open year-round with paid entrance April–September (€4 non-residents, €2.50 Vlaams-Brabant residents) and offers rowboats, pedalos, minigolf, a tourist train and two age-segregated playgrounds.
quote: Rowboats and pedal boats available April–September, €8 per 30 minutes... Minigolf: €4 per person... Tourist Train: €3 per ride.

claim: The outdoor swimming pool at Provinciaal Domein Huizingen has been closed since 1 May 2022 due to renovation costs and sustainability concerns; a natural water play area is planned as replacement.
quote: The outdoor swimming pool at Provinciedomein Huizingen has been closed since May 1, 2022, due to expensive renovation of technical installations and the swimming pool itself.

claim: Vlaams-Brabant's cycling node network spans 2,150 km across Groene Gordel, Hageland, Pajottenland and Dijleland; the Pajottenland & Zennevallei sub-network alone covers 410 km with 70 nodes.
quote: Vlaams-Brabant has an extensive cycling network of 2,150 km... the cycling network Pajottenland and Zennevallei is 410 kilometers long and has 70 cycling nodes.

claim: The Pajottenland walking node network was recently expanded by 290 km of digital routes covering Affligem, Dilbeek, Liedekerke, Roosdaal and Ternat, totalling ~900 km of paths.
quote: walking in the Pajottenland is available on 900 kilometers of walking paths, with the network recently expanded by 290 km of digital routes in municipalities including Affligem, Dilbeek, Liedekerke, Roosdaal, and Ternat.

claim: The Wolfsputten walking route (the Dilbeek nature reserve commonly meant when locals say 'Wolvenberg') offers 8.6 km or 4.6 km loops from the Cultuurcentrum Westrand car park through 90 ha of grasslands and forest with a viewing platform overlooking the Atomium.
quote: Two route options are available: 8.6 km (full route) and 4.6 km (shortened version)... This 90-hectare nature reserve is one of the most important in Flanders... The trail includes a suspended viewing platform offering vistas of the Atomium and Basilica of Koekelberg in the distance.

claim: Coloma Rose Garden in Sint-Pieters-Leeuw houses over 3,000 rose varieties on 60,000 bushes across a 15-ha park, free entry, open Tue–Sun 9–20 (Apr–Sep), with peak bloom June through early October.
quote: more than 3,000 rose varieties from 25 countries bloom on a 15-hectare Coloma Park... approximately 60,000 rose bushes produce an impressive palette of colors and scents.

claim: Kravaalbos in Asse/Opwijk/Aalst-Meldert is an 80-ha forest with three marked loops (yellow 3.2 km, blue 3.8 km, red 4.2 km) plus an 8 km knooppunten-linked route, known in spring for wood anemones and wild hyacinths.
quote: Three marked walking loops are available (yellow = 3.2 km, blue = 3.8 km, and red = 4.2 km). Additionally, the Kravaalbos walking route of just under 8 km guides you around via the walking junction points.

claim: The Groene Gordelroute is a 126 km signposted cycling loop around Brussels' green belt that passes through the Pajottenland and Zoniënwoud, dividable into half-day segments via the knooppunten network.
quote: The Groene Gordel iconic cycling route is a 126 km long cycling route that takes you in a loop through the green belt of Brussels.

claim: Planckendael ZOO 2026 day tickets: adults €37.50 regular / €40.50 peak / €32.50 winter; children under 3 free; €3 off adult and €2 off child when booked at least 1 day in advance.
quote: Adults (18+) pay €37,50 during regular season, €40,50 during peak season, or €32,50 during winter. Children under 3 enter for free... If you buy tickets at least one day in advance, you get €3 off adult tickets and €2 off children's tickets.

claim: Planckendael zoo is open 365 days a year; standard opening is 10:00 (members may enter from 09:00).
quote: The zoo is open 365 days a year. The standard opening time for regular visitors appears to be 10 am, though members with a membership pass are allowed to enter one hour earlier than day-trippers, already welcome from 9 am.

claim: Walibi Belgium (Wavre) advance-booked tickets from €48; €54 for visitors >1.40 m, €44 for 1–1.40 m, free under 1 m; parking €12.
quote: For advance bookings (3 days before), prices are €48 per person... Visitors over 1.40m tall pay €54, while those 1-1.4m tall pay €44, and children under 1m have free access. Parking at the Walibi lot costs €12.

claim: Walibi Belgium opens roughly 10:00–18:00 off-season and 10:00–19:00 in summer (later during Summer Nights), with 50+ rides ranging from gentle kids' attractions to extreme coasters; address Boulevard de l'Europe 100, 1300 Wavre.
quote: Opening hours are usually 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. in summer (often until 10:30 p.m. during 'Summer Nights'); 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. out of season or on weekdays... The address is Boulevard de l'Europe 100, 1300 Wavre.

From March 14 to June 30, 2026: 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM (last entry 5:00 PM); From July 1 to August 31, 2026: 9:30 AM to 7:00 PM; From September 1 to September 30, 2026: 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM. From October 1, 2026 to January 3, 2027, the park is open from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

claim: Mini-Europe individual rates: adults from €21.70 online / €25 on-site; children under 12 from €15.30 online / €17.90 on-site; under 115 cm free.
quote: Adults: From €21.70 online or €25.00 on-site; Children (under 12): From €15.30 online or €17.90 on-site... Children smaller than 115 cm are free of charge and do not need an entrance ticket.

claim: Atomium 2026: open daily 10:00–18:00 (last entry 17:30); closed 19 Jan–6 Feb 2026 for annual maintenance; adults €16, children under 12 €8, seniors 65+ €14, free under 6.
quote: The Atomium is open every day from 10am to 6pm... The Atomium is closed from January 19th to February 6th 2026 for annual maintenance. The standard ticket for adults is €16, reduced tickets for children under 12 and seniors over 65 are €8 and €14 respectively.

claim: The Huizingen outdoor pool has been closed since 1 May 2022 and is being replaced by natural-water play and bathing areas.
quote: The outdoor swimming pool in Provinciedomein Huizingen has been closed since May 1, 2022 due to expensive renovation of technical installation and the pool, and its unsustainable use due to chlorine and high energy consumption.

claim: Train World is at Prinses Elisabethplein 5, 1030 Schaarbeek; open Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00, closed Mondays, last admission 15:30.
quote: Prinses Elisabethplein 5, 1030 Schaarbeek, Belgium... Tuesday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM with last admission at 3:30 PM. The museum operates the same hours Wednesday through Sunday, and remains Closed on Mondays.

claim: Train World tickets: €15 adults, €11 ages 6–17, €5 ages 4–5, free under 4; included in the Brussels Museum Pass.
quote: Tickets cost 15 euros for adults, 11 euros for children ages 6 to 17, 5 euros for children ages 4 to 5, and are free for kids younger than 4... Train World is part of the Museum Pass.

claim: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken open to the public 17 Apr–10 May 2026; €7 entrance, free under 12; tickets online only, sales start 20 March; 5 May reserved for reduced-mobility visitors.
quote: The Royal Greenhouses of Laeken are open to the public from Friday 17 April 2026 to Sunday 10 May 2026... The entrance ticket costs €7.00 and is free for children under 12. Ticket sales start on 20 March at 1 p.m. It is not possible to buy or book tickets on site... 5 May will be dedicated to visitors with reduced mobility.

claim: CityKids indoor playground at Chaussée d'Ixelles 33/35, 1050 Brussels: 1,700 m² for ages 0–12; open Tue–Sun without reservation; under-1 free, 1–2 yrs €9.50, 3–12 yrs €13.50, first two adults free, extra adult €5.
quote: Chaussée d'Ixelles 33/35, 1050, Bruxelles... Children 0-12 months: Free; Children 1-2 years: €9.50; Children 3-12 years: €13.50; First two accompanying adults: Free; Additional adults: €5 each.

claim: Public Aquarium of Brussels (Koekelberg, Avenue Emile Bossaert 27): adults €8.50, children over 1 m up to 15 yrs €6, under 1 m free; ~47 tanks, ~250 species, with stools to help small children see in.
quote: Adult tickets are EUR 8.5, children over 1 meter in height (up to 15 years) are EUR 6, and children below 1 meter in height enter free... The aquarium has 47 tanks exploring fishes, amphibians and invertebrates... with altogether about 250 different species represented.

claim: CityKids spans 1,700 m² in central Brussels and combines a large play structure, ninja course, toddler zone and a separate baby area for ages 0–12.
quote: A brand-new indoor playground called City Kids has opened in the centre of Brussels, covering an impressive 1,700 m² and bringing together play, movement and experience... City Kids offers a complete indoor playground experience for children aged 0 to 12 years.

claim: The Magritte Museum is currently running a dialogue exhibition pairing René Magritte with Jean-Michel Folon
quote: The Magritte Museum is creating a dialogue between the fascinating world of René Magritte (1898-1967) and the poetic creations of Jean-Michel Folon (1934-2005).

claim: Single entry to the Old Masters or Magritte museum is 10 euros, combo ticket 15 euros, and entry is free every Wednesday afternoon and for under-18s
quote: Single entry to the Oldmasters or Magritte museums costs 10 euros for adults and is free for kids aged 18 and younger; combo tickets cost 15 euros for adults.

claim: AfricaMuseum in Tervuren is open 10:00-17:00 on holidays, closed Mondays, with free admission on the first Wednesday afternoon of every month
quote: On school holidays and public holidays, the museum is open from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m... The museum is closed on Mondays, January 1, May 1, and December 25.

claim: Horta Museum admission is 8 euros for adults, 4 euros student/senior, and free on the first Sunday of the month
quote: Adults pay €8; students and seniors €4; primary and secondary school children €2.50. Additionally, entry is free on the first Sunday of the month.

claim: MIM Brussels charges 15 euros adult, 13 euros senior, free for under-18s and Brussels Card holders, with multimedia guides included
quote: Adults (19-64 years): €15... Children under 18 enter for free, as do Brussels Card holders and European disability card holders... Multimedia guides are included in the entrance fee.

claim: Comic Art Museum charges 14 euros adult, open Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-18:00, housed in Horta's Waucquez warehouse with permanent show A Century of Belgian Comics
quote: Tickets cost 14 euros... for adults, 11 euros... for children age 12 to 25 and 6 euros... for children age 6 to 11... open from Tuesday till Sunday from 10 am to 6 pm.

claim: M Leuven introduced updated pricing in April 2026 with free entry for under-18s and free admission for Leuven residents on the first Thursday evening of each month
quote: M introduced updated pricing in April 2026. Admission is free for visitors aged 18 and under... Leuven residents benefit from a reduced admission rate and are welcome to visit M free of charge on the first Thursday evening of each month.

claim: M Leuven shows Valérie Mannaerts: Antennae (3 April-30 August 2026) and Els Nouwen: Oxomoron (30 January-22 November 2026), both on view in May-June 2026
quote: Valérie Mannaerts: Antennae will be running from April 3 to August 30, 2026... Els Nouwen: Oxomoron runs from January 30 to November 22, 2026.

claim: Hof van Busleyden Mechelen permanent exhibition is set in 1507 and showcases the Mechelen Choir Book and the Enclosed Gardens collection from the Burgundian Netherlands era
quote: permanent exhibition set in 1507 that explores Mechelen's rich heyday as the capital of the Burgundian Netherlands... the beautifully illustrated Mechelen Choir Book to the unique collection of Enclosed Gardens.

claim: Many Brussels museums offer free entry on the first Sunday of each month, including 3 May and 7 June 2026
quote: The first Sundays of the month in 2026 are: January 4, February 1, March 1, April 5, May 3, June 7, July 5, August 2, September 6, October 4, November 1, and December 6.

claim: Dilbeek to Leuven is approximately 31 km, placing M Leuven just at the 30 km radius edge, while Tervuren is about 15 km and Mechelen about 23 km away
quote: The distance between Dilbeek and Leuven is 31 kilometers (19 miles) in Belgium... from Dilbeek, Tervuren is 15 km away and Mechelen is 23 km away.

claim: Lotto Brussels Jazz Weekend 2026 runs 22-23-24 May with free jazz across Brussels city squares — the weekend before the target dates.
quote: Lotto Brussels Jazz Weekend (22 - 23 - 24 May) unveils its line-up: three days of free jazz in Brussels' most attractive city squares

claim: Kunstenfestivaldesarts runs 8-30 May 2026 across 24 Brussels venues — final weekend overlaps Saturday 30 May.
quote: Kunstenfestivaldesarts 2026 — Programme — Friday, May 8, 2026 to Saturday, May 30, 2026

claim: Brussels Iris Festival 2026 is 9-10 May, three weekends before the target — past by the trip date.
quote: The Iris Festival will return on 9 and 10 May 2026

claim: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken open to the public only 17 April - 10 May 2026 — closed by the target weekend.
quote: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken open to the public from 17 April to 10 May

claim: Bodegems-h-ART, a free open-air art walk in Sint-Martens-Bodegem starting at Huisje Mostinckx, runs 25 May - 1 October 2026 — perfectly timed for the target weekend.
quote: Bodegems-h-ART, an inspiring art walk runs from May 10 to October 1, bringing art and nature together in a unique experience

claim: Brussels Street Photography Festival (BSPF) 10th-anniversary edition runs 28-31 May 2026 at the Bourse, Halles Saint-Géry and City Hall, with Josef Koudelka receiving the Lifetime Achievement Award on 30 May.
quote: BSPF – 28 – 31.05.2026 in Brussels … Photographer Josef Koudelka will receive the festival's Lifetime Achievement Award during a special evening at the City Hall of Brussels on 30 May 2026.

claim: Les Nuits Botanique festival runs 14-31 May 2026 with 100+ acts across three Botanique stages — including a 30 May bill featuring Ibeyi and Nubya Garcia.
quote: Les Nuits 2026 — May 14 to May 31, 2026 … May 30: Ibeyi will perform with Nubya Garcia

claim: The 46th 20 km door Brussel race takes place Sunday 31 May 2026, starting 10:00 at Jubelpark — currently sold out.
quote: 20 km de Bruxelles – 20 km door Brussel … Sunday, May 31, 2026

claim: Leuven hosts a large Friday market (07:00-13:00, Mgr. Ladeuzeplein / H. Hooverplein) with food, textiles, flowers, and a Saturday city-centre market (09:00-18:00) featuring artisans, antiques, brocante, and specialty food.
quote: Friday market 7:00-13:00 … food, textiles, flowers & plants … Saturday market 9:00-18:00 … artisanal market, antiques & brocante, food

claim: Brussels weekly markets running every weekend include the Marolles flea market at Place du Jeu de Balle (daily 07:00-13:00), Sablon antiques market (Sat 09:00-17:00, Sun 09:00-15:00) and the Gare du Midi market (Sundays from 07:00).
quote: Marolles flea market at Place du Jeu de Balle opens daily from 7am to 1pm … Sablon antiques market is open on Saturday from 9 am till 5 pm and on Sundays from 9 am till 3 pm

claim: Mechelen's Hanswijkprocessie 2026 happens Sunday 10 May with a 150th-anniversary 'Maria, een kroon' theme — before the target weekend, not during.
quote: Hanswijkprocessie zondag 10 mei 2026 - MARIA, een kroon in Mechelen
